display_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Sourced primarily from the Stags Leap District, this Cabernet Sauvignon serves as the younger sibling to the iconic Hillside Select. It bridges the gap between the supple fruit of the valley floor and the structural intensity of the eastern volcanic hillsides.",
  "wine_summary": "One Point Five represents the transition of leadership from John Shafer to his son Doug, but the liquid remains a benchmark for the Stags Leap District's specific power. The wine avoids the bruising tannins of Northern Napa by utilizing the district's unique wind patterns. Cool air from San Pablo Bay funnels through the Stags Leap palisades, slowing ripening and preserving acidity despite an alcohol level that regularly exceeds 15%.",
  "terroir_expression": "The wine draws its character from the iron-rich volcanic soils and Bale loam found at the base of the Stags Leap palisades. These well-drained, rocky sites produce the signature black cherry and cassis profile that defines the AVA. Because the heat is moderated by afternoon breezes bouncing off the rock faces, the tannins develop a plush, velvety texture rather than the gritty, aggressive grip found in higher-elevation mountain fruit.",
  "vinification_summary": "Extensive aging in 100% new French oak barrels for 20 months provides the structural framework necessary to support such high-extract fruit. The winemaking team employs a long maceration—leaving the skins in contact with the fermenting juice—to maximize color and tannin extraction. This process ensures the wine can withstand the oak impact, resulting in integrated notes of cedar, tobacco, and dark chocolate that complement the primary black fruit.",
  "food_pairing": "Pair with dry-aged ribeye with a blue cheese crust to allow the fat to soften the 15.3% ABV. Smoked brisket with a black pepper rub works because the wine’s graphite notes mirror the char of the meat. For a casual option, Nashville hot chicken provides a spicy counterpoint that the wine's high fruit concentration can handle, though the heat will amplify the alcohol. Truffle risotto with shaved parmesan also works well, as the wine's acidity cuts through the heavy cream and butter.",
  "comparable_wines": "Chimney Rock Stags Leap District Cabernet Sauvignon — similar provenance and plush tannin structure. Cliff Lede Stags Leap District Cabernet Sauvignon — shares the same district-driven floral lift and dark fruit density.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with velvety tannins and intense black fruit concentration",
  "cellar_recommendation": "While approachable upon release due to its fruit density, this wine hits its peak at 7 to 10 years. Store at a constant 55 degrees to prevent the high alcohol from oxidizing the delicate floral secondary notes.",
  "value_assessment": "$140 is the standard entry price for this bottle, placing it directly against heavyweights like Caymus Special Selection or Joseph Phelps Cabernet Sauvignon. It is worth the investment because it offers a more site-specific expression of Stags Leap than generic valley-wide blends, providing a clear sense of place that cheaper Napa Cabs lack.",
  "market_position": "Collectors and high-end steakhouse patrons are the primary audience for this label. It occupies a critical spot on wine lists as a reliable 'name brand' that delivers consistent quality across vintages, making it a safe but prestigious choice for business dinners.",
  "insider_take": "Skip this wine if you prefer the herbal, lean profile of traditional Bordeaux; this is unabashedly ripe, high-octane California Cabernet. The real tradeoff here is power for subtlety, but unlike many of its peers at the $150 mark, it maintains enough acidity to keep the 15.3% alcohol from feeling heavy or cloying on the finish.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,

parsed.hook: Sourced primarily from the Stags Leap District, this Cabernet Sauvignon serves as the younger sibling to the iconic Hillside Select. It bridges the gap between the supple fruit of the valley floor and the structural intensity of the eastern volcanic hillsides.
parsed.wine_summary: One Point Five represents the transition of leadership from John Shafer to his son Doug, but the liquid remains a benchmark for the Stags Leap District's specific power. The wine avoids the bruising tannins of Northern Napa by utilizing the district's unique wind patterns. Cool air from San Pablo Bay funnels through the Stags Leap palisades, slowing ripening and preserving acidity despite an alcohol level that regularly exceeds 15%.
parsed.terroir_expression: The wine draws its character from the iron-rich volcanic soils and Bale loam found at the base of the Stags Leap palisades. These well-drained, rocky sites produce the signature black cherry and cassis profile that defines the AVA. Because the heat is moderated by afternoon breezes bouncing off the rock faces, the tannins develop a plush, velvety texture rather than the gritty, aggressive grip found in higher-elevation mountain fruit.
parsed.vinification_summary: Extensive aging in 100% new French oak barrels for 20 months provides the structural framework necessary to support such high-extract fruit. The winemaking team employs a long maceration—leaving the skins in contact with the fermenting juice—to maximize color and tannin extraction. This process ensures the wine can withstand the oak impact, resulting in integrated notes of cedar, tobacco, and dark chocolate that complement the primary black fruit.
parsed.food_pairing: Pair with dry-aged ribeye with a blue cheese crust to allow the fat to soften the 15.3% ABV. Smoked brisket with a black pepper rub works because the wine’s graphite notes mirror the char of the meat. For a casual option, Nashville hot chicken provides a spicy counterpoint that the wine's high fruit concentration can handle, though the heat will amplify the alcohol. Truffle risotto with shaved parmesan also works well, as the wine's acidity cuts through the heavy cream and butter.
parsed.comparable_wines: Chimney Rock Stags Leap District Cabernet Sauvignon — similar provenance and plush tannin structure. Cliff Lede Stags Leap District Cabernet Sauvignon — shares the same district-driven floral lift and dark fruit density.
parsed.style_profile: Full-bodied dry red with velvety tannins and intense black fruit concentration
parsed.cellar_recommendation: While approachable upon release due to its fruit density, this wine hits its peak at 7 to 10 years. Store at a constant 55 degrees to prevent the high alcohol from oxidizing the delicate floral secondary notes.
parsed.value_assessment: $140 is the standard entry price for this bottle, placing it directly against heavyweights like Caymus Special Selection or Joseph Phelps Cabernet Sauvignon. It is worth the investment because it offers a more site-specific expression of Stags Leap than generic valley-wide blends, providing a clear sense of place that cheaper Napa Cabs lack.
parsed.market_position: Collectors and high-end steakhouse patrons are the primary audience for this label. It occupies a critical spot on wine lists as a reliable 'name brand' that delivers consistent quality across vintages, making it a safe but prestigious choice for business dinners.
parsed.insider_take: Skip this wine if you prefer the herbal, lean profile of traditional Bordeaux; this is unabashedly ripe, high-octane California Cabernet. The real tradeoff here is power for subtlety, but unlike many of its peers at the $150 mark, it maintains enough acidity to keep the 15.3% alcohol from feeling heavy or cloying on the finish.
